clue.text: A lift for one in the army

indicators.note: in places the numeral word inside the word for a large body of soldiers

parts.note: a host is an army, as in the heavenly host
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone in the forces is offered a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; HOST, an old word for an army, takes I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoisting is raising, so a hoist is a lifting device or a boost upward.

clue.text: Trees, the focus of lots of pleasure

indicators.note: the focus of puts the trees at the centre of the word for lots

parts.note: haps are lots in life, chance fortunes
pines are evergreen trees

explanation.surface: A woodland at the centre of much enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: HAPS, old words for chances or lots in life, have PINES placed at 'the focus of' them.
explanation.definitionFit: Happiness is a state of contentment and joy, close in sense to delight.

clue.text: Idol — give him a generous part

indicators.note: part says the answer is a portion of the words him a generous

explanation.surface: An instruction to give a heroic figure a big role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' takes letters from 'hIM A GEnerous'; 'give' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a worshipped likeness, a carved figure or icon.

clue.text: It's not commonly inferior, being unmarked

parts.note: in dialect, it is not becomes 'tain't
less can mean lower in rank or worth

explanation.surface: Something informal and second-rate turns out spotless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tain't is a dialect contraction of 'it ain't'; 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without a taint is free of stain or blemish, so spotless.

clue.text: Post centre has no right working on Whit Sunday …

indicators.note: working suggests the letters being reworked into a new order
has no tells us to drop a letter from the word centre

explanation.surface: A sorting office is short-staffed but still open on a church holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no right' removes R from CENTRE to leave CENTE; 'working' rearranges POST plus CENTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Whit Sunday is the Christian feast celebrating the Holy Spirit's descent, seven weeks after Easter.

clue.text: Mrs Grundy, say, taking the Gospels etc to be wise

parts.note: Mrs Grundy is a byword for a narrow-minded, easily shocked person
NT is the New Testament, which contains the Gospels and more

explanation.surface: A prim woman takes up the Bible to become sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Grundy, an offstage character in an 18th-century play, stands for prudish British respectability. 'taking' and 'to be' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prudent means acting with care and good judgement, as a sensible person does.

clue.text: Composer confused lines with points

indicators.note: confused suggests the letters of lines being jumbled

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: A musician gets muddled over staff lines and dots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges LINES to NIELS; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer of six symphonies.

clue.text: Invest daughter with enough to provide permanent support

indicators.note: invest in the sense of clothe, so the word for enough wraps the daughter

parts.note: enow is an archaic word for enough

explanation.surface: Parents put money into a daughter's future.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'invest' someone is to clothe them, so ENOW, an archaic word for enough, wraps D. 'with' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow a college or chair is to give a fund that pays for it in perpetuity.

clue.text: Frank finished without any definite conclusion

parts.note: frank means open or candid
ended means finished

explanation.surface: An honest person has ended a discussion that resolved nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-ended describes something with no fixed limit or outcome.

clue.text: A poor state, in a sense

indicators.note: poor suggests the word state being in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A country in poor condition, in some respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges STATE; 'A' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses, alongside sight and hearing.

clue.text: . and its first letter has room for an obvious remark

parts.note: its refers back through the dots to the previous clue's answer, whose initial is P
room in the sense of scope or freedom to move

explanation.surface: The continuation of the previous clue: the feast's initial makes space for a banal comment.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots link this clue to 4 across: 'its first letter' is the first letter of that answer, P. 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trite, overused statement offered as if it were insightful is a commonplace.

clue.text: Non-U compulsion to bring into line

indicators.note: Non-U tells us to take the letter U out of the word for compulsion

parts.note: duress is coercion or compulsion

explanation.surface: An unrefined urge to make everyone conform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' is also a British term for socially unrefined, from the U and non-U class debate; here it simply drops U from DURESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers dress ranks when they align themselves in a straight row.

clue.text: Clumsy to write back about it? On the contrary

indicators.note: about, reversed by 'On the contrary', means the word it goes around the writing word rather than inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means the word for writing is turned round

parts.note: to pen is to write

explanation.surface: Someone awkwardly asks whether to reply about something, then contradicts themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Normally the reversed writing word would go 'about' the other; 'On the contrary' flips the container, so the pronoun goes around it instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, the same as awkward or bungling.

clue.text: Were heels built up at this place? No

indicators.note: built up suggests the letters being assembled into a new structure

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether heels were raised here, and is told not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built up' rearranges the nine letters of WERE HEELS. The definition is the denial: not at this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere other than here means in another location, the denial of being at this spot.

clue.text: Sulphur, for example, giving out heat in a fire

definitions.meaning: sulphur is one of the chemical substances in the periodic table

definitions.text: giving out heat in a fire
definitions.meaning: an electric fire has a heating coil that glows when switched on

explanation.surface: A chemist notes sulphur releasing heat as it burns.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulphur is a chemical element, and the glowing heating coil of an electric fire is also called an element.

clue.text: Mill, say, for oriental company with clear prospects

parts.note: E for east, the oriental direction
clear views mean there is no mist

explanation.surface: A mill owner works for an eastern firm with good prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: John Stuart Mill was a 19th-century political economist. 'for' and 'with' are link words; clear prospects have NO MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stuart Mill wrote Principles of Political Economy, a classic of the dismal science.

clue.text: Mother is in agreement with one about vagrant

indicators.note: is in places the word for mother inside the word for agreement

parts.note: a nod signals agreement
ma is a familiar word for mother
one is the Roman numeral I
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A mother agrees with someone about a wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant moves from place to place, just as wandering tribes do with no fixed home.

clue.text: Preserve and spoil French invalid

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
malade is French for ill, or a sick person

explanation.surface: A conserve and a ruined sick person in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus jam, a kind of conserve.

clue.text: Accountant's girl is unbelievable

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective while the answer is a name, a prophet nobody believed

parts.note: CA, a chartered accountant, plus the possessive 's
Sandra is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An accountant's girlfriend is incredible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word; the definition describes a person, used loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Trojan prophetess was cursed so that her true warnings were never believed.

clue.text: Backer gets odds on thus? Right

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds when a race begins
taken as written
so means thus

explanation.surface: A punter checks the betting odds and is told they are correct.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is the betting odds on a horse at the off. 'gets' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor financially supports an event or person, so is their supporter.

clue.text: "The Price of Freedom," by English writer

parts.note: a ransom is the price paid to free a captive

explanation.surface: A book title followed by its English author.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons. 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome was an English author of children's books such as Swallows and Amazons.

clue.text: With Tarquin's ravishing _____" (Macbeth)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Macbeth's dagger speech, where murder moves like Tarquin with long silent steps

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth's line is 'With Tarquin's ravishing strides, towards his design / Moves like a ghost'; the missing word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Shakespeare's line means long steps or paces.

clue.text: Stage accessories for part of the act with lines

parts.note: a scene is a division of an act in a play
RY, railway, is the abbreviation for railway lines

explanation.surface: Props for one section of a play with spoken lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'with' are link words; 'lines' looks theatrical but means railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Painted backdrops and set pieces on a theatre stage are its scenery.

clue.text: I. for example, go to church to give judgement

parts.note: the word I is a first-person part of speech that stands in for a noun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A person heads off to church to deliver a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like a person but is a grammatical example; 'go to' is a link word joining it to CE, the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to declare formally, as a judge pronounces sentence.

clue.text: Cut back on fruit

definitions.meaning: to trim a plant or reduce something

explanation.surface: Advice to eat less fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune is to trim or reduce, and a prune is a dried plum.

clue.text: Cat at one time round the bend

indicators.note: round says the word for formerly goes around the bend

parts.note: once means at one time
a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: A cat once went crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the bend' looks like British slang for mad; here 'round' wraps ONCE around U, a U-shaped bend.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat of Central Asia.

clue.text: A capital scent

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name for Rome, Italy's capital

explanation.surface: A city with a distinctive smell.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant smell, the same as a fragrance or odour.

clue.text: Part of a sonnet to a group of musicians

definitions.meaning: the opening eight lines of a Petrarchan sonnet

explanation.surface: A poem set to music for a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are sets of eight: the first eight lines of a sonnet and an eight-piece ensemble.

clue.text: Jack's wedding

definitions.meaning: the word that belongs before Jack in the name of the British flag

explanation.surface: Two words about a man named Jack getting married.
explanation.walkthrough: The Union Jack is the British national flag, so the answer is what 'Jack' has in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The British flag is called the Union Jack, and a marriage is a joining of two people in matrimony.

clue.text: Some bowling, feat journalist exaggerated

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
an act is a deed or feat
ED, an editor, is the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is impressed by a bowling performance and overstates it.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an OVER is a set of six balls from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Overacting is playing a part too broadly, so the performance was overdone.

clue.text: See about ten metre free-style — very much so

indicators.note: about tells us the bishop's seat goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see
ten is the Roman numeral X

indicators.note: free-style suggests the letters of metre swimming in any order

explanation.surface: Someone watches a ten-metre freestyle swim, very impressed.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; ELY is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire. 'free-style' rearranges METRE to TREME, and ELY goes 'about' X plus TREME.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely means to a very great degree, an intensifier like hugely.

clue.text: Beyond the ordinary run

definitions.meaning: more than is normal or usual
in cricket a run scored from a wide or no-ball is not credited to the batter

explanation.surface: A remarkable run.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a run from a wide or no-ball counts for the team but not for any batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional goes past the usual amount, and in cricket a bye or wide is a bonus run.
